notes.2: Serves 12. Mince the parsley a bunch at a time.

move.title: A green salad made with a knife
move.body: In Lebanon, tabbouleh is mostly parsley, with just a little bulgur. Today you'll mince two big bunches of parsley fine and even with a chef's knife, rocking the blade, then dress it with lemon and olive oil.

callback.body: If you made fattoush, you chopped herbs and vegetables into pieces you could fork up. A mince is much finer: bits about the size of a grain of rice, small enough that the parsley turns into a fluffy green salad.

why.title: Dry herbs cut clean
why.body: Wet leaves stick to the knife and bruise into a dark paste instead of cutting into crisp, bright bits. Spin or blot the parsley until it's completely dry before it touches the board.

why.title: Rock the blade
why.body: Keep the tip of the knife on the board and rock the heel up and down while your other hand rests flat on the spine. The tip never lifts, so the blade can't jump, and your fingers stay on top, away from the edge.

why.title: Cut once, not over and over
why.body: Every pass of a dull edge crushes the leaves and squeezes out their juice. A sharp, honed knife and a pile gathered tight cuts each leaf once or twice, so it stays green and fresh.

why.title: Bulgur soaks, it doesn't cook
why.body: Bulgur is wheat that's been cooked and dried, then cracked. Fine bulgur only needs hot water to soften, so the salad never sees the stove.

why.title: Let it sit
why.body: Ten minutes after dressing, the bulgur soaks up lemon and the parsley softens a little. Much longer and the tomatoes start to weep, so it's best within a few hours.

wrong.sign: The parsley turned dark and mushy
wrong.fix: It was wet, or it got chopped too many times. Dry the next batch completely and gather the pile before each pass.

wrong.sign: The bits are uneven, some big leaves left
wrong.fix: Gather the pile back together and rock through it again, just the big pieces.
Pour on 2 more tablespoons of hot water, cover, and wait 5 minutes.
Add salt and lemon a pinch and a squeeze at a time, tasting after each.

quiz.q: Why must the parsley be completely dry?
choices: Wet leaves bruise into paste instead of cutting clean
quiz.explain: Dry leaves cut into crisp, separate bits.

quiz.q: When you rock-chop, what stays on the board?
quiz.explain: Your other hand rests flat on the spine, on top.

choices: About the size of a grain of rice
About the size of a pea
quiz.explain: A small dice is about ¼ inch; a mince is finer.

steps.text: Put the bulgur in the small bowl. Heat the water in the microwave until it boils, pour it over the bulgur, and cover the bowl with the plate.
While it soaks, rinse the parsley and mint in the colander. Shake them, then roll them up in the kitchen towel and press until the leaves are completely dry.
Pull the parsley leaves off the thick stems. Thin stems near the leaves can stay. Pull the mint leaves off their stems.
steps.tip: Save the parsley stems for stock (Unit 8), or throw them away.

steps.text: Gather a handful of parsley into a tight pile. Rock the chef's knife through it, tip on the board and your other hand flat on the spine, then gather the pile and rock through again until the bits are about the size of a grain of rice. Mince the rest the same way and put it in the large bowl.
steps.look: Fluffy, bright green bits, no whole leaves and no dark paste.
steps.tip: Wipe the blade clean with your finger from the spine side, never along the edge.

steps.text: Mince the mint the same way and add it to the bowl.
Quarter the tomatoes, scoop out the seeds, and dice them into ¼-inch cubes: strips, then across. Add them to the bowl.
Trim the root ends off the green onions. Line them up and slice them as thin as you can, white and green parts both. Add them to the bowl.
Fluff the bulgur with the fork. Taste a few grains: they should be tender. Add it to the bowl.
Pour in the lemon juice and olive oil, and add the salt and pepper. Toss gently with the spoon until everything is coated.
Let the salad sit, then taste it. Add more salt or lemon if it needs it, and serve.
steps.tip: It keeps in the fridge for a day, but it's best the day it's made.
